tile-installation/bradenton.title: Tile Installation Bradenton FL | Showers & Floors
tile-installation/bradenton.description: Tile installers for kitchen and bath remodels in Village of the Arts, Cortez and Perico Island homes in Bradenton, FL. 2026 pricing.
tile-installation/bradenton.lede: Most of our Bradenton tile work rides along with a bigger renovation in the Village of the Arts or Cortez, where a kitchen or bath gets redone as part of turning an old bungalow into someone's first home.
tile-installation/bradenton.capsule: Tile installation in Bradenton is concentrated in kitchen and bath remodels tied to full-house renovations in the Village of the Arts and Cortez historic district, alongside newer waterfront work at Perico Island and Harbour Isle. Typical 2026 installed ranges run $6 to $22 per sq ft, with wet-area waterproofing priced separately from field tile.
tile-installation/bradenton.body_html:
The Village of the Arts and Cortez historic district see a steady flow of first-time buyers and investors turning over 1920s and 1950s bungalows, and tile installation on those jobs almost never happens on its own — it's the kitchen backsplash and bath floor getting done alongside new plumbing, paint and often a new subfloor where the original wood has failed. Cortez in particular still has working fishing-village character to it, and a lot of the renovation work there respects that with simpler, classic tile formats rather than anything trend-driven. We run the same TCNA-spec substrate prep on these older slabs as we would on new construction, since a fifty-year-old slab with hairline cracks needs crack-isolation membrane just as much as a fresh pour does.

Perico Island and the newer waterfront pockets near Harbour Isle are a different scope: primary bathrooms with a Schluter Kerdi or Wedi shower system, and large-format porcelain in open living areas that face the water. These homes are close enough to the Manatee River and Anna Maria Sound that flood-zone exposure factors into the waterproofing spec, not just the shower.

Downtown, riverfront addresses along Wares Creek and the Riverwalk corridor carry AE flood zone designations, which is one more reason porcelain and stone hold up better there than anything with a fiber-cement backer near grade. If you searched flooring installers near me from Cortez or the Village of the Arts, we run the same crew across both markets. Our tile installation page covers lippage control and shower-pan options in more depth, and our post on which floor tile isn't slippery when wet is worth reading before choosing a finish for a bath that sees a lot of foot traffic. A cracked tile from settling in an older Bradenton slab is a common floor repair call once the grout starts failing around it.
tile-installation/bradenton.cost_html: A Village of the Arts bungalow retiling a 120 sq ft kitchen and bath in 12-to-18-inch ceramic runs $6 to $10 per sq ft, a typical 2026 installed range of $720 to $1,200, and a Kerdi or Wedi shower rebuild in the same job adds $1,800 to $3,800. A 500 sq ft Perico Island living-area retile in large-format 24-inch porcelain runs $9 to $15 per sq ft, or $4,500 to $7,500 installed. Regrouting existing tile instead of replacing it runs $3.50 to $7.00 per sq ft. These are typical 2026 ranges for Manatee County, not quotes; the free in-home estimate confirms substrate condition before pricing is final.

faqs.q: Do you install tile as part of a full Village of the Arts renovation?
faqs.a: Yes, most of our tile work there is exactly that, kitchen and bath tile installed alongside plumbing, paint and sometimes subfloor repair on a bungalow being fully renovated, rather than a standalone tile job.

faqs.q: What shower system do you recommend for Perico Island homes?
faqs.a: Schluter Kerdi or Wedi waterproofing systems, given the proximity to the Manatee River and Anna Maria Sound. Both hold up better against long-term moisture exposure than a traditional mortar-bed shower pan.

faqs.q: Is a fifty-year-old Cortez slab ready for large-format tile?
faqs.a: Usually, once we've checked it. Older slabs can have hairline cracks that need a crack-isolation membrane before large-format porcelain goes down, which we confirm during the free estimate rather than assuming either way.
